proof:
Source: Step 1 and the Notation paragraph of the parent proof (J smooth, J(P) = 1 + |P|^2/2 + O(|P|^4), hence D^2J(0)[Q,Q] = |Q|_HS^2, and Legendre ellipticity by continuity), with the computation written out. Notation: fix n, l. L = L(R^n, R^l) with operator norm; e_1..e_n the standard basis of R^n; G(P) in Mat_n(R), G(P)_{ab} =

; J(P) = sqrt(det(I + G(P))); D^2J(P)[Q][Q'] := fderiv R (fderiv R J) P Q Q'. 1. Positivity. G(P) is symmetric and for xi in R^n, xi^T G(P) xi = sum_{a,b} xi_a xi_b

= |P(sum_a xi_a e_a)|^2 >= 0. Hence xi^T (I + G(P)) xi >= |xi|^2 > 0 for xi != 0, so I + G(P) is positive definite and det(I + G(P)) > 0 (Mathlib Matrix.PosDef.det_pos). 2. Smoothness (assertion (i)). Each entry P ->

is the continuous bilinear inner product composed with the continuous linear maps P -> P e_a, P -> P e_b, hence C^infinity on L. So P -> I + G(P) is C^infinity into the finite-dimensional matrix space and D(P) := det(I + G(P)) is C^infinity (det is a polynomial in the entries). By step 1, D(P) > 0 for all P, and sqrt is C^infinity on (0, infinity); hence J = sqrt o D is C^infinity on L. 3. Quadratic part along lines. Fix Q in L, put S := G(Q) and tau := tr S = sum_a |Q e_a|^2. For s in R, det(I + sS) = 1 + s tau + s^2 r(s) with r a polynomial (Mathlib Matrix.det_one_add_smul). Put phi(s) := sqrt(1 + s tau + s^2 r(s)); phi is C^infinity near s = 0 (the radicand is 1 at s = 0), phi(0) = 1 and phi'(0) = tau/2. Since G(tQ) = t^2 S, we have J(tQ) = phi(t^2) for t near 0. Hence f(t) := J(tQ) satisfies f'(t) = 2t phi'(t^2) and f''(t) = 2 phi'(t^2) + 4 t^2 phi''(t^2) near 0, so f''(0) = 2 phi'(0) = tau. 4. Second derivative at 0. J is C^2, so by the chain rule along t -> tQ, f''(t) = D^2J(tQ)[Q][Q]; thus D^2J(0)[Q][Q] = sum_a |Q e_a|^2. 5. Comparison with the operator norm. For h = sum_a h_a e_a with |h| = 1, |Q h| <= sum_a |h_a| |Q e_a| <= (sum_a h_a^2)^{1/2} (sum_a |Q e_a|^2)^{1/2} = (sum_a |Q e_a|^2)^{1/2} (Cauchy-Schwarz). Taking the sup over h: ||Q||^2 <= sum_a |Q e_a|^2 = D^2J(0)[Q][Q]. 6. Continuity of D^2J in components. Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L and c_L > 0 with |pi_r(Q)| <= c_L ||Q|| for the coordinate functionals pi_r (Q = sum_r pi_r(Q) E_r; finite dimension). Since J is C^2, each P -> D^2J(P)[E_r][E_s] is continuous. Put err(P) := c_L^2 sum_{r,s} |D^2J(P)[E_r][E_s] - D^2J(0)[E_r][E_s]|; err is continuous with err(0) = 0 and, by bilinearity, |D^2J(P)[Q][Q'] - D^2J(0)[Q][Q']| <= err(P) ||Q|| ||Q'|| for all Q, Q'. (This avoids any norm on the space of bilinear forms.) Choose eps > 0 with err(P) <= 1/2 whenever ||P|| <= eps. 7. Conclusion (assertion (ii)). For ||P|| <= eps and Q in L: D^2J(P)[Q][Q] >= D^2J(0)[Q][Q] - err(P)||Q||^2 >= ||Q||^2 - (1/2)||Q||^2 = (1/2)||Q||^2, by steps 4-6. Together with step 2 this proves the statement. QED Lean note: step 6 needs continuity of P ↦ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) P E_r E_s. One route avoids the bilinear-form type: for J of class C^2, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) P Q' Q = fderiv ℝ (fun P' => fderiv ℝ J P' Q) P Q' (fderiv_clm_apply with the constant second argument Q, then simp; checked at the pin), and P' ↦ fderiv ℝ J P' Q is a C^∞ map L → ℝ, so P ↦ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) P E_r E_s is continuous. Lean note (checked at the pin, Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c): at the default maxSynthPendingDepth, instance synthesis fails for every algebraic and normed structure (even AddCommGroup) on the bilinear-form type (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ. With `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3` Lean synthesizes AddCommGroup, Module ℝ, NormedAddCommGroup, NormedSpace ℝ and FiniteDimensional ℝ for it, and (d⁻¹ • (a (x + d • e) - a x)) P Q = d⁻¹ * (a (x + d • e) P Q - a x P Q) closes by simp. The alternative, used in the argument above wherever possible, is to work only with the scalar components x ↦ a x P Q (values a x E_r E_s on a basis E_1..E_N of L), which needs no structure on that type.
key_steps: Gram matrix G(P) is positive semidefinite, so det(I + G(P)) > 0
J = sqrt(det(I + G(P))) is C^infinity on L
det(I + sS) = 1 + s tr S + O(s^2) gives D^2J(0)[Q][Q] = sum_a |Q e_a|^2
continuity of the components P -> D^2J(P)[E_r][E_s] yields eps with error <= 1/2
